All is only valid for a Workstream and cannot retain an operation. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: RemoveParams
inputSchema.description: A client key requests data-only removal; omission keeps irreversible removal's consent path.

RemoveScope.description: Which contents the user chose to remove from a Workstream.

tool.name: rail_rename

tool.name: reaction_create
tool.description: Save a named instruction that a declared condition (named Agents finished, a PR's checks passed, or one instant) delivers once to a target Agent as a Message. Creates immediately without approval, recording you as the authenticated maker. Needs a nonempty one-line `reason` explaining why it is needed (separate from the delivered instruction), an `operation` retry key, an `expires_at` and a target that is you or in your Reach; the definition is immutable, so to change it stop it and create another. A refusal saves nothing. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: CreateParams
inputSchema.description: `reaction.create`: the caller's Actor comes from its connection, never from here.

operation.description: The caller's retry key: the same operation and payload answer with the first definition.

target.description: The Agent id the instruction is sent to.

instruction.description: The exact words delivered as one Message at each firing.

max_firings.description: Finite and positive; the default is one. Above one needs `rearm` on an Agents condition.

rearm.description: Re-arm after a firing; only an Agents condition may.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 with its UTC offset, later than now.

reason.description: Why this Reaction is needed: one nonempty line, trimmed before saving and retry comparison.

Condition.description:
What a reaction waits for. `agents` combines Agent ids only; a PR's checks and one instant are
separate conditions.

oneOf.description: One to twenty distinct Agents finished: every one, or with `any` the first.

The required checks of a named PR's head passed. `repository` is `host/owner/name`; the PR is the
one the target Agent's Worktree holds, and its head is pinned at activation.
One explicit instant: RFC 3339 with its UTC offset, and what to do when it is missed.

LatePolicy.description: NR6: what a missed instant does once, before expiry.

tool.name: reaction_preview

inputSchema.title: PreviewParams
inputSchema.description:
NR6 `reaction.preview`: a civil date, time and UTC offset the user typed. There is no zone name: an
offset is the only form with no ambiguous or nonexistent local time.

inputSchema.title: RunParams
inputSchema.description: `reaction.run`: spends one remaining firing; `operation` makes a retry return the first result.

Start a login shell in a Terminal owned by a Workstream that is yours or in your Reach; `workstream` is required for Agents. The answer holds its `terminal_id`. Use your own tools for commands; open a Bubble only when the user needs to see its output or will interactively type into it. Routine builds, tests and inspection use your own tools. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: OpenParams
inputSchema.description: X12: start the user's login shell, owned by `workstream` or the Project when absent.

cols.description: U4590: initial PTY columns; absent keeps the hostless 80-column default.

rows.description: U4590: initial PTY rows; absent keeps the hostless 24-row default.

tool.name: terminal_open
terminal_read
tool.description: Read a Terminal's output you have not read yet, as plain text; `next` is the offset after it. At most 200 lines and 16 384 bytes a call, `truncated` says more remains. With `after`, read from that offset instead and keep your place.

inputSchema.title: ReadParams
inputSchema.description: X13, X16: `terminal.read`. New output as plain text: from `after`, or from `reader`'s cursor.

after.description:
Read from this offset (a `next`, or the `offset` of a screen); the cursor stays as it was.
Absent: read from `reader`'s cursor and move it to `next`.

max.description: Lowers the 16 384-byte cap of the reply, which also holds at most 200 lines.

tool.name: terminal_resize

tool.description: Read a Terminal's screen as it is now, as plain text, with the `offset` to read from next. Only the Terminals of your Runs and your Workstream. Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

tool.name: terminal_search

Agent references accept `me` (you), an exact case-sensitive Rail name, `name:<Rail name>` for collisions, or a canonical id. Owner fields also accept explicit Actors; omitted/null Todo owners remain Unassigned.

inputSchema.title: SearchParams
inputSchema.description: X13: `terminal.search`. The lines of the output log that match a regular expression.

pattern.description: A regular expression (Rust `regex` syntax), matched against each line.

after.description: Search from this offset; the log's start when absent.

max.description: Lowers the 16 384-byte cap of the reply.

inputSchema.title: AssignParams

tool.name: workstream_rewind
tool.description: Rewind one child (`agent`) or every child of your Workstream to a Checkpoint you wrote. The turns after it leave each rewound Agent's context. `files` is `keep` to leave every file as it is, or `restore` to return each Worktree to its state at the Checkpoint; commits, pushes and Issues are never undone. A child that started after the Checkpoint leaves the Rail and keeps its Worktree.

inputSchema.title: RewindParams
inputSchema.description: `workstream.rewind`. `files` is required. `agent` selects one child, as in `RewindPlanParams`.

Files.description: What happens to files: `keep` leaves every file, `restore` returns each selected Worktree to its Mark.

tool.name: workstream_rewindPlan
tool.description: Read what rewinding your Workstream to one of your Checkpoints would do, changing nothing: for each child (one named by `agent`, or all), whether it started after the Checkpoint and so would leave the Rail, and the files changed since.

inputSchema.title: RewindPlanParams
inputSchema.description:
`workstream.rewindPlan`: what a rewind of the Door's own Workstream to `checkpoint` would do.
`agent` selects one child, direct or nested; without it every child is selected.
